newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Police shooting of Frenchman indefensible - wife.
newsitem.headline: Police shooting of Frenchman indefensible - wife.

text.p: The Australian widow of a knife-wielding Frenchman shot dead by police on Bondi Beach said on Wednesday the killing was morally indefensible and called for an independent inquiry into his death.
Melinda Dundas said her husband Roni Levi, 33, was not a violent person and did not suffer from a mental illness or drug addiction, despite media portrayals of him as mentally unstable.
"Irrespective of Roni's condition on the beach, the actions of the two police officers are indefensible," Dundas told reporters at a press conference.
"Whether this shooting can be defended legally is unclear, but morally it can not. The violence was excessive and appalling. It is unjustifiable," she said.
Levi, a photographer, was shot four times in the chest by two policemen in a dawn confrontation on Saturday on Bondi Beach, Australia's most famous beach. He died in hospital.

Senior police officers have said the killing resulted from a failure in police procedures, but have not specified the nature of the failure and have announced compulsory re-training of police to deal with disturbed people.

Levi's family in France and Australian civil liberty campaigners have criticised the killing, charging police with overreacting. An internal police investigation is underway, as well as a coronial inquiry.
Dundas said the two officers, who would have been a blur to her husband because he was not wearing his glasses at the time of the shooting, should be suspended pending the inquiries.
"The current police policy is effectively shoot-to-kill and clearly this is wrong and has to be changed," she said.
"We hope that the coroner will ensure that this matter is properly investigated. That it is both an independent and impartial inquiry so that those responsible are brought to justice..."
